keep.quote: In mice, the spaces between brain cells open up by about sixty per cent during sleep, and the waste washes out faster (c12).

About a hundred years ago, in 1924, two people were tested, and they forgot less after sleeping than after the same hours awake (c13). And in rats, the day's activity replays in sleep, faster than real time (c14).
Brain cells in a dish, wired to the old bat-and-ball video game, began to get better at it within five minutes (c19).
